title: Bricktop's moves to a bigger club; Cole Porter as regular
summary: She took over a larger cabaret near Place Pigalle with head waiter Jimmy Marsellini; Cole Porter attended nightly in season, and she hired Freddy Johnson's band and a vocal choir with Mabel Mercer.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And she was so successful, that within a year, she had to expand. She had to expand, so she contacted a cabaret on the corner of Place Pigalle. It was called the Pigalles. No, not the Pigalles, there was another name. Pigalles was opposite. It doesn't make any difference. De Monaco, that was the name. I don't remember the name of the proprietor, but she contacted her. The proprietor of the cabaret -- I'll
explain it to you, the way it was. If you walk up Pigalle, Rue Pigalle from Rue Fontaine, you see where you're at?
It's on the lefthand side. The corner of the Le Place Pigalle.
Before you get to the square.
And you -- I don't remember -- Mr. Taudisac (?) was the proprietor of the place.

She made arrangements with him, to take over his place. It was a much bigger place. She redecorated and everything, and opened, and she had gotten a head waiter, whose name was Jimmy Marsellini, an Italian fellow.

He was a very, very fine head waiter, and he knew almost everybody, the smart set, because he always worked in the establishments like the Cafe de Paris, and Maxim's and, you see. So, she had everything her way at the time, you see. And one of her regular clients was Cole Porter.

Yes, Cole Porter. He would be there in the Spring, from the Spring, say around May, until the end of September or October. He would be there every night. And she opened, she had Freddie Johnson to form an orchestra, she hired Freddie Johnson, she hired me, all individually, and her husband, Peter du Conge, she hired a very fine saxophone player, who was with the Buffalos, his name was Nelson Kincaide.
Well, I know Dean Kincaide. I know a fellow named Dean Kincaide.

It might be his brother. I know Nelson. Nelson was a little older than I was. And a terrific musician. A fine saxophone player, he would play a wonderful first saxophone, semi-balance, you know. Don't ask him to put a note that is extra, not an extra note. Everything that is written would be played, just -- and he was one for arrangements. And he arranged to have a choir when she opened, she had a choir of eight persons. You've heard of Mabel Mercer?
Well, Mabel Mercer was one of the singers.
